counterexample.initialized_ticks: -100 (liquidityNet +L1), -20 (liquidityNet +L2) and 100 (liquidityNet -(L1+L2)), from positions over [-100, 100) with L1 and [-20, 100) with L2
counterexample.note: The iterator comes new from initDown, so currentTick is 0, and reset returns before setting it. hasNext is true because 0 > -50, so the walk returns tick 0, which is not initialized, then -20. Active liquidity at -50 is L1, but the walk ends at L1 - L2. A second failure: with initialized tick 100, start 105 and end 50, the walk returns [105, 100] instead of [100], because an unaligned start is returned as a tick when its floor tick's bit is set.

new_flaw.description: The patch moved the currentTick assignment below the empty-range return. When start equals end, reset leaves currentTick unchanged: 0 for a new iterator from initDown, or wherever the earlier pass stopped when the hook calls reset again. At a negative tick, hasNext is then true and the walk returns ticks above the current price.
new_flaw.scenario: Tick spacing 10, pool at tick -50 with active liquidity L1 from [-100, 100). An attacker adds a position over [-20, 100) with liquidity L2 larger than L1, which does not change active liquidity at -50. A trader makes the first taxed zero-for-one swap of a block and the tick stays at -50. initDown(-50, -50) leaves currentTick at 0, so CompensationPriceFinder.getZeroForOne visits ticks 0 and -20, and liquidity.sub(L2) reverts the swap. With a smaller L2 the swap goes through with wrong liquidity, and if the first pass returns early, the second pass after reset continues from the stale position and adds reward growth to ticks that were never crossed.

summary: Checks the bitmap bit of the start's floor tick and skips the advance when it is set, leaving currentTick at the start tick. For an unaligned start this returns the start tick itself, which is not an initialized tick, and the patch also moved the currentTick assignment below the empty-range return, so start equal to end can leave a stale currentTick.
